chunks: Ali ibn Unsur from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Abdullah ibn Bayser from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

A man came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said, 'O Messenger of Allah! I bear the greatest weight that men bear. Is it permissible for me to go to some of the beasts that belong to me, a she-camel or a donkey, for the women are not strong enough to bear what is with me?' The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'Verily, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, did not create you until He created for you from your form that which can bear you.'

So the man left, and he did not delay long before he returned to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and said to him the same as his words from the first time. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to him, 'So where are you from the Black, the long-necked one?'

So the man left, and he did not delay long before he returned and said, 'O Messenger of Allah! I testify that you are truly the Messenger of Allah. I sought what you ordered me with, so I copulated with my own form from that which bears me, and that has sufficed me.'

key_terms.السَّوْدَاء: The Black (a specific woman known by this epithet)
key_terms.العَنَطْنَطَة: Long-necked (a description of a specific woman)
key_terms.يَحْتَمِلُنِي: That which can bear me (referring to physical capacity for intercourse)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a man with great strength having intercourse with animals according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the principle of natural compatibility (fitrah) in marital relations, where the Prophet (peace be upon him) advises a man of exceptional strength to seek a partner whose physical constitution can naturally accommodate him, rather than forcing a mismatch. In Shia scholarly tradition, this narrative is often cited to emphasize that Allah’s creation is purposeful and balanced, serving as a practical guideline for marital harmony and a metaphor for spiritual compatibility. The resolution underscores the Islamic view that divine wisdom is embedded in physical form, making the 'black, sturdy' woman (al-Sawda’ al-Anatnata) a symbol of suitable endurance.
